newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia sees huge LNG demand in Asia-Pacific.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia sees huge LNG demand in Asia-Pacific.

text.p: Indonesia's state oil company Pertamina said on Thursday demand in the Asia-Pacific region for liquefied natural gas (LNG) would rise to more than 90 million tonnes a year by 2005 from about 59 million tonnes this year.

"LNG demand in the Asia-Pacific region is expected to be between 58 and 59 million tonnes in 1996 (and) is forecast to exceed 90 million tonnes per year by 2005," Pertamina's general affair director Baharuddin told an oil and gas seminar.
"However, now we are seeing some new demand forecasts of 120 million tonnes by 2005 and 160 million tonnes by 2010," he said.

Baharuddin said Japan would remain the dominant market for LNG in the Asia-Pacific region with imports of 46 million tonnes in 1996, 50 million to 55 million tonnes by 2000 and between 65 million and 70 million tonnes by 2010.
However, he said the growth of demand in South Korea and Taiwan would be even more impressive, with a potential increase of up to 25 million tonnes by 2010.
He said Thailand, China and the Philippines were also expected to join the group of LNG importers.
Baharuddin said the existing capacity of LNG plants operating in the Asia-Pacific region was around 64 million tonnes.

"Gas demand in the Asia-Pacific region has grown rapidly during the last decade and will continue to grow for two reasons. First, overall energy consumption is expanding. Secondly, natural gas is becoming the energy of choice for many users," he said.
He said Indonesia, the world's biggest LNG exporter, would soon build another LNG plant to meet future demand.
Indonesia exports more than 20 million tonnes of LNG a year, mainly to Japan. Other LNG significant producers include Malaysia, Brunei, Abu Dhabi, Australia and Alaska.
